statement: For every integer n >= 1, let L_n be Shoji's two-bridge link C(1^(2n+1)) and let P_n be its Q-polynomial after removal of its Laurent monomial factor, exactly as fixed in problem.md. Every zero of P_n is real; in fact, every zero is simple and lies in [-3,1]. Thus the frozen universal assertion in source.md is proved in its full scope.
contribution: A complete proof of the odd-length analogue posed in Shoji's Remark 4.5. A direct three-state rational-tangle Q-skein transfer derives the odd recurrence and all distinct initial Laurent polynomials; a Chebyshev closed form and an all-n sign-interlacing grid prove the result. Exact Sturm computations for 1 <= n <= 20 independently audit the symbolic formulas. Current targeted searches found no inspected primary source already resolving the odd case, but no claim of exhaustive novelty or priority is made.
